content.title: USA beats Dominican Republic 2-1 to reach WBC championship game: Live updates and reaction
content.text: Follow live reaction after the powerhouse matchup in Miami lived up to the hype.Mason Miller and Aaron Judge (right) hug in celebration at reaching the WBC final. Getty ImagesUSA silences Dominican bats — and criticsFor the past two weeks as the World Baseball Classic has unfolded, the stars assembled by Team USA have talked about this tournament as if unsure how to gauge its importance. Bryce Harper lamented that the WBC is not the Olympics. Tarik Skubal opted to make one start before departing the team. Mark DeRosa spoke before a crucial game as if he didn’t understand the rules. Their celebrations sounded muted compared to the boisterous displays of the other participants.All it took to turn up the volume was a date with the Dominican Republic.In a 2-1 semifinal victory over the D.R. on Sunday evening at loanDepot Park, Team USA displayed a level of performance and verve that met the moment and set the stage for the team to win the WBC for the second time in three iterations of the tournament. The Americans will face the winner of Monday’s semifinal between Italy and Venezuela.When Team USA returns to the field Tuesday, questions about the group’s level of interest in this exhibition will be gone. They answered those on Sunday.Read more below.‘Last pitch an exclamation point’ Getty ImagesThe emails have been coming in too, mostly discussing how that semifinal in Miami ended. Here is a quick sample …💬 Jerry: “Obviously I haven’t seen them all, no one has, but this WBC has to rank as one of the worst ball and strike umpiring series in the history of baseball. From the first game to tonight’s, it’s been terrible — against all teams — with the last pitch tonight being the exclamation point.”💬 Darko Orsic: “What a horrendous way to end a beautiful game. The third strike … NOT. EVEN. CLOSE. Shameful way for the USA to win. Even they have to be embarrassed.”A reminder that our inbox is always open, so please do get in touch: live@theathletic.comA famous D.R. fan weighs inKarl-Anthony Towns, star center for the NBA’s New York Knicks who’s of Dominican heritage and was supporting the D.R. team in the World Baseball Classic, had a direct (and vulgar) response when asked about the final strike three call.Shocking statistic Getty ImagesAmong this lineups full of All-Stars, only one player recorded a multi-hit game tonight. That was Ketel Marte. The Dominican second baseman and No. 2 hitter, who plays for the Arizona Diamondbacks, had two hits — one of which still resulted in the third out when Aaron Judge threw out Fernando Tatís Jr. trying to go from first to third.AL East showed out tonight Getty ImagesAll three home-run hitters in tonight’s game play in the American League East — Junior Caminero for the Tampa Bay Rays, Gunnar Henderson for the Baltimore Orioles and Roman Anthony for the Boston Red Sox. New York Yankees captain Aaron Judge nearly hit a third for Team USA if not for a perfectly-timed home run robbery from Julio Rodríguez. Toronto Blue Jays superstar Vladimir Guerrero Jr. had to settle for being stranded on third base after a double, while his new Blue Jays teammate Tyler Rogers induced a Juan Soto double-play ball to get out of a fifth-inning jam.Your views: All eyes on final call Getty ImagesHere’s what you had for us in the discussion page as Team USA saw off Dominican Republic in a tight one — and yes, the talk was dominated by that final strike call … 💬 Darko O: “Absolute embarrassment on the last call of the game. Not even close. Great game stolen by cheap call. Shameful. USA MLB players will have to be ‘I’m sorry’-ing their DR MLB teammates for the sad way they were eliminated.”💬 Qtkellen2013: “To say the DR got screwed and lost bc of that one call is loser behavior. Average 10 runs and you score once? I think that’s why they lost.”💬 Paul D: “Great game! Very proud of US players.”💬 D D: “Agree ABS should be implemented and that was a ball … But people do realize the ball mark they show on TV isn’t where the pitch crosses the plate, right? That ball was in the zone pretty damn late and is a tough call to make for a breaking ball.”Remember, you can join the discussion right here and you can always send your thoughts to us in an email too: live@theathletic.comSkenes roars after final outPaul Skenes is notoriously not one to show emotion — so when he does, it’s worth noting, like here after the final out recorded by Team USA tonight.More from Paul SkenesPaul Skenes on his opponents tonight:💬 “The Dominican Republic is the toughest lineup I ever faced, for sure. I think they would probably say the same thing about facing us.”Dominican Republic will rue missed chances The Dominican Republic had nine batters reach base tonight — and the only man not left on bade was Junior Caminero, courtesy of his home run. The powerhouse Dominican lineup had:Bases loaded, two out on the fourthRunners on first and second, one out in the fifthRunners second and third, one out in the seventhRunner on second, one out in the ninthAnd failed to score each time. Yes, there were a couple of questionable strike calls in those sequences, but still stunning from such a talented group of hitters.DeRosa is pro-ABSDespite his team benefitting from a blown strike three call at the end of tonight’s game, Mark DeRosa said he’s a fan of the new challenge system that would overturn such calls in the future, starting with the upcoming MLB regular season.💬 “I would assume it comes in next (World Baseball Classic). I’m a fan of it.”DeRosa praises bullpen Imagn ImagesTeam USA manager Mark DeRosa on his bullpen:💬 “That was high-level baseball at its finest.”DeRosa also confirmed that Nolan McLean will start Tuesday’s championship game.Semifinal LVP Getty ImagesNow, Gregory Soto was truly less valuable: he faced two hitters and gave up the game-winning homer. But Fernando Tatís Jr. impacted this game in a couple less obvious ways.In the third inning, after reaching on a fielder’s choice, Tatís was thrown out by Aaron Judge trying to go first to third on a Ketel Marte single. Had Tatís held up at second, the D.R. would have had Juan Soto up with two on and two outs.In the fifth, Tatís singled, and then Marte singled again. This time, Tatís held up at second, though it seemed like he had a much better chance that time of reaching third safely. Soto grounded into an inning-ending double play.Then, in the seventh, with runners on second and third and U.S. reliever David Bednar on the ropes, Tatís swing and missed at three splitters, striking out on four pitches. Bednar escaped.Anthony: ‘Italy scare woke us up’ Getty ImagesWhat happens next and how does the U.S. win this World Baseball Classic? Roman Anthony has thoughts …💬 “Just continue to be relentless, continue to do what we’ve been doing so well. We had a little scuffle there with Italy and that really woke us up, and we understand now that we’re playing something for more than just ourselves. We’re playing for the best country in the world, and to be able to go out there and represent this country and these fans, it’s everything for us. “So we’re gonna stay within ourselves, we gonna play a great brand of baseball and we’re gonna take it one pitch at a time.”Pujols on 2028 OlympicsAlbert Pujols says he wants to manage the Dominican Republic in the 2028 Olympics, which DR has qualified for.💬 “Always. Every time I have the chance to wear this jersey, I’ll do it with pride to represent my country. Once again, thank God that we gave our country that possibility to be in the Olympics in 2028. “Of course, God willing I will be there, but right now this is not my main goal. Talking about the game, what happened, thinking about my guys and the great job that they did.”Let’s hear from Albert Pujols Getty ImagesThe first question Dominican Republic manager Albert Pujols was asked during his postgame press conference was about tonight’s strike-zone umpiring. He responded in Spanish:💬 “I’m not going to focus on that last pitch. It was a huge game between two huge teams and I’m super proud for the guys that represented us in this classic. Once again, we represented our homeland in this world classic, we raised our flag and we left our brand. Our country should feel proud.”Pujols was asked about the strike zone again in English, and he replied in English:💬 “I just said it in Spanish. I don’t want to focus on the last pitch. Obviously didn’t go our way. Disappointed about the way that the game ends. But I don’t want to criticize any of that. It just wasn’t meant to be for us.”Brutal stretch for Dominican Republic Getty ImagesThe Dominican Republic enters each World Baseball Classic expecting to dominate, and for good reason, given how much elite baseball talent comes out of the Caribbean nation and how central the sport is to its culture. And that talent has consistently shown up for the WBC, with several players and even manager Albert Pujols, one of the best hitters of all time and a future Hall of Famer, equating this to a World Series (which Pujols won twice).Yet since Team D.R.’s dominating run through the 2013 WBC the superstar-laden squad has not even returned to the final. The Dominicans lost to Team USA in the quarterfinals of the 2017 tournament, suffered a stunning group-stage exit in 2023, and now lost to the U.S. again, this time in the semifinal round.Anthony on his WBC ‘blessing’ Getty ImagesIt didn’t necessarily feel like it at the time, but Roman Anthony hit the winning homer — and it secured another incredible memory for what has been a bonus throughout for the Boston Red Sox. Speaking to Fox Sports, Anthony said … 💬 “Yeah, it’s been a blessing just to represent this country. It was something for me going into spring training, I didn’t expect it. Heading into my first full year, I thought I was going to be in Fort Myers the entire time, and then when I got the call, it was a no brainer. “And to be here, to be around these guys around this staff, everyone around me, it’s been unbelievable. An honour to represent this country.”And on that winning shot …💬 “When I hit it, I kind of just blacked out. I was in my head just, please go. Please go!”Semifinal MVP Getty ImagesI’ll give this to Roman Anthony, whose fourth-inning homer was the difference in this game. Dominican manager Albert Pujols had just gone to the bullpen to bring in a lefty, Gregory Soto, to face the lefty Anthony. The 21-year-old Anthony waited out three balls, sized up two center-cut sinkers and pounded the third one over the center-field wall.Reviewing our picks to click Getty ImagesDominican Republic 1B Vladimir Guerrero Jr. ❌Good as this guess felt when Guerrero scorched a 116.1 mph double to left field, that was all he managed to do at the plate in this game. He went 1 for 4, ending the WBC batting .444 with a 1.420 OPS.United States DH Kyle Schwarber ✅Schwarber didn’t provide either of the two swings that mattered for Team USA — the Gunnar Henderson and Roman Anthony solo shots — but he singled and walked, reaching base twice to push his tournament OPS to 1.000.
